title: Accounts Payable Manager
description:
The Nuclear Company is the fastest growing AI tech-enabled startup in the nuclear and energy space, pioneering a fleet-scale approach to building the next generation of nuclear reactors. Through our design-once, build-many model, we're accelerating the deployment of safe, reliable, and affordable nuclear energy.

We operate with an AI-first mindset. Every employee is expected to leverage AI, technology, and the Nuclear Operating System (NOS) as integral components of their role to improve the quality, speed, and impact of their work. We expect every team member to continuously identify opportunities to automate workflows, enhance decision-making, improve processes, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of NOS as a strategic operating capability that enables The Nuclear Company to scale with excellence.

We hire people who are driven by purpose, thrive in ambiguity, and are energized by building what has never been built before. Our team combines intellectual curiosity with high agency, embraces candid feedback and continuous learning, and holds themselves and others to exceptional standards. Our values—Transparency, Responsibility, Unity, Scrappiness, and Tenacity—guide how we hire, collaborate, and make decisions every day. They are not words on a wall; they are the standard by which we operate. TRUST is the foundation of our safety culture, fostering intellectual honesty, accountability, and open communication, while our values challenge every team member to execute with urgency, humility, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to our mission.

About the role

The Accounts Payable Manager will play a critical, hands-on role in building and running the company’s accounts payable operations as The Nuclear Company continues to grow. As the first dedicated AP resource, this position will own the end-to-end payables process, invoice processing, payment execution, vendor management, expense and corporate card administration, reconciliations, and AP close with a strong focus on accuracy, timeliness, financial controls, and fraud prevention.

Working closely with Accounting, Procurement, Treasury, and business leaders, the Accounts Payable Manager will design, implement, and scale the processes, controls, automation, and reporting the function needs. As the organization moves into construction-phase activity, this individual will stand up the project payables infrastructure—purchase order workflows, contractor payment processes, retainage, and compliance documentation required to support significantly higher volume and complexity.

Note: This is a hybrid position based in our downtown Columbia, South Carolina office. The role has been posted in Charlotte and surrounding markets for visibility, as the hybrid schedule may make the commute workable for candidates living outside the immediate Columbia area. Candidates should be within commuting distance of Columbia or open to relocation.

Role Responsibilities

  • Accounts Payable Operations: Own the end-to-end AP process across a multi-entity structure, including invoice processing, coding, approvals, payment execution, intercompany payables, account reconciliation, and resolution of invoice or payment discrepancies, ensuring accuracy and timely execution.
  • Procure-to-Pay Design: Partner with Procurement to build and administer scalable purchase order workflows—PO policy, approval routing, match thresholds, and receiving—so payables keep pace with contract-driven and construction-phase spend.
  • Vendor Management: Own vendor onboarding and master data, including W-9/1099 compliance, banking detail verification, and supporting documentation; respond to payment and account inquiries and resolve discrepancies.
  • Payment Processing & Fraud Prevention: Manage payment cycles in accordance with vendor terms, contractual requirements, internal approvals, and company policies; design and enforce payment fraud controls, including banking-change verification, positive pay, and payment release protocols.
  • Expense & Card Administration: Administer the travel, expense, and corporate card program, ensuring transactions are appropriately documented, coded, and approved.
  • Construction & Project Payables: Build and run construction-phase payables workflows ahead of site activity—pay applications, retainage tracking, lien waivers, and contractor compliance documentation—in coordination with Project teams and Procurement.
  • Month-End & Year-End Close: Own AP-related close activities, including accruals, account reconciliations, intercompany settlement support, adjustments, and supporting schedules required for accurate and timely financial reporting.
  • Internal Controls & Audit Support: Design and maintain effective controls, procedures, and documentation across AP, including segregation-of-duties design with the Controller; provide AP-related schedules and documentation in support of internal and external audits.
  • AP Reporting, Automation & Systems: Use AI tools and automation to drive touchless invoice processing, exception-based review, and clear visibility into outstanding payables and payment activity.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Treasury, Procurement, Legal, and business teams to resolve issues, support vendor and contractual requirements, and ensure payables activity aligns with broader business needs.

Required Experience

  • Experience: 6+ years of progressive accounts payable, accounting, or related finance experience, including experience owning or managing core accounts payable activities.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience in lieu of a degree.
  • Accounts Payable Expertise: Strong hands-on experience across the full AP lifecycle—invoice processing, coding and approvals, payment execution, vendor management, account reconciliation, and discrepancy resolution—including experience in multi-entity or intercompany environments.
  • Accounting Knowledge: Strong understanding of GAAP and the relationship between accounts payable, expenses, cash, and the general ledger, including experience supporting month-end close, accruals, and account reconciliations.
  • Systems: Proficiency with modern cloud ERP required, with hands-on NetSuite experience strongly preferred, along with strong Excel skills.
  • AI & Automation Fluency: Demonstrated use of AI tools and automation in daily work, with experience implementing automated workflows (invoice capture, coding, approvals, reconciliations) that scale operations without proportional headcount growth.

Nice to Have

  • Start-up or high-growth company experience, particularly building or scaling a finance function
  • Construction or project-based payables experience, including pay applications, retainage, lien waivers, and contractor compliance documentation
  • Power, energy, utility, or other regulated industry experience
  • Experience administering T&E and corporate card platforms and their ERP integrations
  • Experience implementing AP automation or invoice capture platforms integrated with ERPs
  • Experience with 1099 reporting and sales/use tax considerations on purchases
  • Experience supporting financial audits and strengthening internal controls and documentation within accounts payable
  • CPA or CMA certification is a plus, but not required

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation packages
  • 401k with company match
  • Medical, dental, vision plans
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays

Estimated Starting Salary Range
The estimated starting salary range for this role is $118,000 - $140,000 annually less applicable withholdings and deductions, paid on a bi-weekly basis. The actual salary offered may vary based on relevant factors as determined in the Company’s discretion, which may include experience, qualifications, tenure, skill set, availability of qualified candidates, geographic location, certifications held, and other criteria deemed pertinent to the particular role.

We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We prohibit discrimination in all aspects of employment, including hiring, promotion, demotion, transfer, compensation, and termination.

The Accounts Receivable Manager will play a critical, hands-on role in building and running the company’s billing and receivables operations as The Nuclear Company continues to grow. The company’s receivables profile is low-volume and high-complexity contract-governed services billings, joint venture cost reimbursements and fees, and intercompany settlements, so this role centers on billing accuracy, contract-to-cash discipline, and cash visibility rather than high-volume collections.

As the first dedicated AR resource, this position will design the billing architecture and own customer invoicing, cash application, unbilled receivables tracking, reconciliations, and AR close and reporting. As revenue streams expand and contract complexity increases, this individual will build the receivables processes, controls, and automation required to keep pace without proportional headcount growth.

Note: This is a hybrid position based in our downtown Columbia, South Carolina office. The role has been posted in Charlotte and surrounding markets for visibility, as the hybrid schedule may make the commute workable for candidates living outside the immediate Columbia area. Candidates should be within commuting distance of Columbia or open to relocation.

Role Responsibilities

  • Billing & Contract-to-Cash: Own customer invoicing end to end, ensuring invoices are accurate and issued in accordance with contract terms—including milestone, time-and-materials, and cost-reimbursable structures—and that billing requirements are captured at contract signing in partnership with Legal and Business Development.
  • Accounts Receivable Operations: Manage cash application, account reconciliation, credit adjustments, and resolution of billing discrepancies across a multi-entity structure, ensuring accuracy and timely execution.
  • Intercompany & Joint Venture Billing: Prepare and manage cost reimbursement, fee, and intercompany billings arising from the company’s joint venture and multi-entity structure, including settlement tracking and supporting documentation.
  • Unbilled Receivables & Revenue Coordination: Track unbilled receivables and contract assets, and coordinate with Technical Accounting to ensure billing aligns with revenue recognition (ASC 606) treatment.
  • Collections & Aging Management: Monitor aging and outstanding balances, resolve the documentation, certification, and contract issues that hold up payment, and escalate issues or trends that could impact cash flow.
  • Cash Flow & AR Reporting: Maintain accurate reporting and visibility into receivables, unbilled balances, aging, and expected cash inflows, feeding Treasury’s cash forecasting and providing meaningful insight to Accounting, Finance, and business leadership.
  • Month-End & Year-End Close: Own AR-related close activities, including account reconciliations, adjustments, intercompany settlement support, and supporting schedules required for accurate and timely financial reporting.
  • Internal Controls & Audit Support: Maintain effective controls, procedures, and documentation across billing and receivables operations; provide AR-related schedules and documentation in support of internal and external audits.
  • Automation, Process & Systems Improvement: Use AI tools and automation to streamline invoicing, cash application, and reporting; evaluate and improve AR workflows as the business evolves; partner with Business Systems on data flows between NetSuite and operational platforms, including NOS.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Treasury, Legal, Sales & Business Development, and Project teams to resolve issues, support customer and contract requirements, and ensure receivables activity aligns with broader business needs.

Required Experience

  • Experience: 6+ years of progressive accounts receivable, billing, or related accounting and finance experience, including experience owning or managing core AR or billing activities.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience in lieu of a degree.
  • Billing & AR Expertise: Strong hands-on experience across the full receivables lifecycle with emphasis on contract-based invoicing—milestone, time-and-materials, or cost-reimbursable billing—plus cash application, account reconciliation, and discrepancy resolution, including experience in multi-entity or intercompany environments.
  • Accounting Knowledge: Strong understanding of GAAP and the relationship between receivables, revenue, unbilled balances, and cash, including working familiarity with revenue recognition concepts (ASC 606) sufficient to partner effectively with Technical Accounting.
  • Systems: Proficiency with modern cloud ERP required, with hands-on NetSuite experience strongly preferred, along with strong Excel skills.
  • AI & Automation Fluency: Demonstrated use of AI tools and automation in daily work, with experience implementing automated workflows (invoicing, cash application, reporting) that scale operations without proportional headcount growth.

Nice to Have

  • Start-up or high-growth company experience, particularly building or scaling a finance function
  • EPC, construction, power, energy, or other project-based industry billing experience
  • Government or cost-reimbursable contract billing experience
  • Experience with complex customer contracts, milestone billing structures, and unbilled receivable / contract asset accounting
  • Experience with NetSuite billing, invoicing, or advanced revenue management modules
  • Experience supporting financial audits and strengthening internal controls and documentation within receivables

About the role

The Nuclear Company is hiring an AI Engineer 1 to build test automation and quality practices for NOS, the Nuclear Operating System, that meet NQA-1 nuclear quality assurance standards. NOS is the software platform behind one of the largest nuclear buildouts in the United States, and every module it ships must meet the rigor that nuclear regulation demands. This role sits at the intersection of software quality, regulatory compliance, and AI-augmented engineering.

This is a hands-on, entry-level role with a clear differentiator: you will use AI as a tool to generate, review, and improve tests, while also developing the skills to test AI-powered systems themselves. You will work alongside the Compliance/Quality/Testing Lead, ramp on NQA-1 requirements and Palantir Foundry, and help establish the verification and validation (V&V) practices that give NOS its regulatory backbone.

Responsibilities

  • Build automated test coverage (unit, integration, and end-to-end) for assigned NOS modules, using AI-assisted generation and review to accelerate coverage and catch gaps.
  • Support NQA-1 documentation efforts for digital systems, help translate regulatory quality requirements into traceable test artifacts and evidence packages.
  • Establish and refine defect tracking and V&V workflows alongside the Compliance/Quality/Testing Lead, ensuring traceability from requirement to test to resolution.
  • Ramp on Palantir Foundry, the NOS architecture, and the team's AI tooling, understanding how data flows through the system and where quality gates apply.
  • Contribute to the team's approach for testing AI-powered features within NOS, prompt regression, output validation, and behavioral consistency checks.

Required Experience

  • Computer science degree or equivalent, with 0-2 years of professional experience (internships, co-ops, and project work count).
  • Test automation fundamentals in at least one modern framework: Playwright, Cypress, Jest, PyTest, or equivalent.
  • Has used AI to generate, review, or improve tests in a real project, not just theoretical knowledge, but hands-on application.
  • Strong fundamentals in at least one backend language (Python or TypeScript preferred).
  • Good written and verbal communication, and willingness to learn the nuclear regulatory environment (NQA-1).

Preferred Experience

  • Coursework or project work testing AI/ML systems or LLM-powered applications (prompt testing, output validation, drift detection).
  • Exposure to regulated industries where quality documentation and traceability are mandatory (nuclear, aerospace, defense, medical, financial).
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and integrating automated tests into build/release workflows.
  • Familiarity with verification and validation (V&V) concepts, requirements traceability, or formal QA processes.
  • Exposure to Palantir Foundry or similar data/ontology platforms.
  • Understanding of version control workflows and code review practices.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation packages
  • 401k with company match
  • Medical, dental, vision plans
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays

The Assistant Controller will play a critical, hands-on role in the organization’s daily accounting operations and financial reporting. Reporting to and working closely with the Controller, this position requires a strong working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), financial analysis, and internal control best practices.

The Assistant Controller will be instrumental in managing the month-end close process, assisting with the preparation of accurate financial statements, and ensuring compliance across transactional accounting activities. In addition, this position will support the accounting and reporting needs of the company’s growing nuclear services business segment.

This role provides an excellent opportunity to develop leadership skills, drive process efficiencies, and contribute to the continued growth of the finance function within a rapidly scaling organization.

**NOTE: This role works a hybrid schedule out of our Washington, DC or Columbia, SC office. Candidates should be within commuting distance of one of these locations or open to relocation.

Role Responsibilities

  • Financial Reporting Assistance: Assist in the preparation of accurate and timely financial statements, including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements. Provide support for financial analysis projects and management reporting.
  • Accounting Operations Execution: Manage the execution of specific accounting functions, such as overseeing the general ledger reconciliation process, reviewing accounts payable and accounts receivable, and ensuring the accuracy of complex journal entries.
  • Month-End and Year-End Support: Execute key tasks within the month-end and year-end close processes, including managing accruals, preparing balance sheet reconciliations, and ensuring timely completion of close activities.
  • Internal Controls and Compliance: Help maintain and enforce effective internal controls across accounting operations. Support the documentation and testing of controls to ensure compliance with financial regulations and company policies.
  • Budgeting and Forecasting Support: Provide supporting data and analysis for annual budgeting and ongoing forecasting processes. Track departmental spending and assist with variance analysis.
  • Nuclear Services Segment Support: Support the accounting and reporting needs of the company’s growing nuclear services business segment. Assist with project/job cost tracking, services revenue recognition, and segment-level reporting and analysis.
  • Audit Coordination: Serve as a key resource during internal and external financial audits, preparing requested documentation and schedules.
  • Process Improvement: Identify and implement improvements to accounting processes, systems utilization, and documentation to increase efficiency and accuracy.

Required Experience

  • Experience: Typically 6–8+ years of progressive accounting experience, with the depth of experience and demonstrated capabilities being more important than years alone. Exposure to corporate and/or public accounting environments is preferred.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Technical Knowledge: Strong understanding of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and financial reporting standards.
  • Software Proficiency: Proficiency with accounting software and ERP systems, along with advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
  • Analytical Skills: Demonstrated ability to perform financial analysis, interpret financial data, and prepare detailed account reconciliations.

  • Start-up or high-growth company experience
  • Power, energy, or utility industry experience
  • Experience supporting large capital expenditure projects
  • ERP implementation experience
  • Services or project-based revenue recognition and job cost accounting experience
  • Audit process implementation experience
  • Big 4 public accounting experience
  • Exposure to public-company reporting requirements

You May Be a Fit If You Have:

  • A track record of digging into financial results, reconciliations, and accounting issues to identify discrepancies and resolve problems at the source.
  • Experience building, documenting, or improving accounting processes and internal controls in an evolving environment.
  • Examples of identifying and implementing process or system improvements that increased accuracy, visibility, or efficiency.

  • Comfort operating in a hands-on environment where you may need to build a process, improve an existing one, or jump into the details to get something across the finish line.

  • A desire to contribute to a mission-driven organization working to bring reliable, clean baseload nuclear power to the world.

TNC Services, the services division of The Nuclear Company, brings together field execution, specialized workforce solutions, and Professional Services expertise to support the nuclear industry across the full asset lifecycle. While The Nuclear Company advances the fleet-scale deployment of new nuclear power, TNC Services supports the industry today through outage and maintenance execution delivered by TNC Field Services and TNC FieldWorks, alongside Professional Services spanning project delivery, engineering, licensing and regulatory, security, cybersecurity and compliance, and workforce development. Together, our teams combine proven nuclear expertise, technology, and an AI-enabled approach to help utilities operate safely and reliably today while building the capabilities needed for tomorrow’s nuclear fleet.

About the role

The Business Development Manager, Services drives new-business identification and early-stage pursuit development across TNC's Services portfolio: Security, Training & Workforce Development, Engineering, Licensing & Regulatory, Program Management, and Field & Union Services. This is the engine room of TNC's pursuit pipeline – you will be originating, qualifying, and advancing leads from initial market signal through a defined qualification standard to a qualified opportunity ready to advance.

This is an individual-contributor role. You will personally own accounts and customer relationships, carry your own qualified-opportunity target, and work horizontally across every service line rather than a single vertical. Coverage is horizontal by design, and the role carries coverage expectations across the portfolio rather than volume alone; quarterly focus across service lines is set with the Director of Sales based on capacity and market signal.

Success is measured on qualified opportunities accepted into the pipeline, pipeline value created, and data integrity at the qualification gate. Business line owners own capture and close; you own everything upstream of the gate, and your qualification number is independently approved rather than self-reported.

Please note: This role requires regular office presence in either Washington, D.C., or Columbia, South Carolina, along with the ability to travel according to business needs. The position may be advertised in additional nearby markets for visibility; however, candidates must be commutable to or willing to relocate to one of the two designated office locations.

Responsibilities

Pipeline Generation & Qualification

  • Identify and qualify new business across the entire TNC Services portfolio, carrying quarterly targets for leads generated and qualified opportunities handed to business line owners
  • Own leads from creation through disposition, meeting the full qualification standard before advancement into the opportunity pipeline
  • Identify cross-selling opportunities into existing accounts, reengage dormant accounts on a targeted cadence, and conduct market and account research to identify white space across assigned accounts

CRM Discipline & Forecasting

  • Own accurate, current data on all assigned accounts, contacts, and leads with stages recorded when there are updates, maintaining accurate next steps, and correct tagging at creation
  • Meet aging and disposition standards to ensure no leads sit in active stages without contact and without documented disposition
  • Contribute to weekly pipeline reviews by providing next steps for each owned lead, as well as proactively surfacing stalled & at-risk leads
  • Surface CRM friction points and usability gaps as a daily user of the platform, contributing practical feedback on fields, stages, and reporting to Business Ops

Relationship & Network Development

  • Build and sustain relationships with technical and economic buyers across operating utilities, DOE sites, OEMs, EPCs, and new-build developers
  • Map the buying group on each account with role-tagged contacts, so decision-maker coverage is documented before handoff
  • Represent TNC at industry events annually, with a pre-event target list and proper documentation of leads generated during the event within the CRM

Cross-Functional Coordination

title: Manual Machinist - Full-Time On Site
description:
Manual Machinist

Employment Type: Direct Hire (Duke Energy Lark Maintenance)

Employment Status: Full-Time | Permanent (Not an outage travel role)

Location: Mount Holly, North Carolina

At The Nuclear Company, we believe building the future of nuclear energy starts with supporting the people who power the industry today. Building on the trusted 25-year legacy of Powerhouse Resources, now part of The Nuclear Company, we continue to support utilities, suppliers, and contractors across the nuclear industry by connecting skilled professionals with meaningful career opportunities.

This opportunity is being recruited by The Nuclear Company on behalf of Duke Energy Lark Maintenance. While most of our services opportunities support outage and field work, this position is a direct-hire opportunity with one of our trusted industry partners.

If selected, you will be hired directly as a full-time, permanent employee of Duke Energy Lark Maintenance. They are responsible for compensation, benefits, payroll, work schedules, supervision, onboarding, workplace policies, and all other terms and conditions of employment.

For this opportunity our role is to identify qualified candidates, coordinate the interview process, and support both candidates and our client throughout the hiring process.

About the role

The Manual Machinist is responsible for the safe setup and operation of manual machining equipment to manufacture, repair, and inspect precision components supporting power generation equipment. This role requires strong hands-on machining experience, the ability to work from technical drawings, and the capability to hold close tolerances while maintaining a strong safety and quality mindset.

This is a full-time, onsite position located at Duke Energy’s Lark Maintenance facility in Mt. Holly, NC, supporting plant operations through TNC Energy Services. The ideal candidate will live/commute to the location daily as relocation is not offered for this position, at this time.

Responsibilities

  • Set up and independently operate manual lathes, milling machines, horizontal and vertical boring mills, grinders, drills, and large metal-cutting saws
  • Machine components to close tolerances (±0.001”)
  • Inspect parts using precision measuring and testing equipment (M&TE)
  • Utilize OD/ID micrometers, Vernier calipers, dial indicators, and hardness testers
  • Read and interpret blueprints, drawings, and work instructions
  • Perform preventative maintenance on shop equipment
  • Maintain shop housekeeping and organization
  • Safely operate forklifts, man lifts, water jets, sandblasters, and oxy/fuel cutting equipment
  • Inspect and utilize overhead cranes up to 60-ton capacity
  • Support safe rigging and lifting of large components

Experience / Required Qualifications

  • Proven manual machining experience
  • Ability to hold tolerances of ±0.001”
  • Proficiency with precision measurement tools
  • Rigging and crane qualification (or ability to obtain)
  • Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Strong safety mindset and positive attitude
  • Powersafe Training (or ability to complete)

Hiring Process

Qualified candidates will be contacted by a recruiter from The Nuclear Company for a brief phone interview. Candidates selected to move forward will interview directly with Duke Energy Lark Maintenance, which is solely responsible for hiring decisions and employment offers. Duke Energy Lark Maintenance administers its own Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) policies and employment practices.

About the role

The Engineering I Program is The Nuclear Company’s early-career engineering program for exceptional graduating seniors who want to help build the next generation of nuclear infrastructure.

We are hiring students graduating in Spring 2027 for full-time roles beginning in Summer 2027.

Engineering One is designed for engineers who want more than a traditional entry-level position. Participants will work alongside experienced engineers, constructors, licensing professionals, project leaders, and Members of Nuclear Staff on real problems tied directly to the development and deployment of nuclear projects.

The program provides broad exposure across the nuclear project lifecycle while building deep technical capability in an assigned discipline. Depending on your background and project needs, you may work across mechanical engineering, civil and structural engineering, construction and project delivery, nuclear licensing, Supply Chain and Procurement, systems engineering, or related technical functions.

  • Mechanical systems and equipment used in nuclear and conventional power facilities
  • Piping, pumps, valves, heat exchangers, pressure vessels, and rotating equipment
  • System design and engineering calculations

description:

TRUST is the foundation of our safety culture, fostering intellectual honesty, accountability, and open communication, while our values challenge every team member to execute with urgency, humility, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to our mission.

About the role

Deploying a fleet of nuclear power plants is one of the most ambitious and consequential undertakings in the global energy transition — and The Nuclear Company is doing it. You will join a small but world-class Applied Research and AI team and work on genuinely hard, open research problems at the intersection of AI and large-scale infrastructure: how do you optimize construction across a fleet of simultaneous sites, allocate capital intelligently under deep uncertainty, and keep a distributed critical infrastructure secure? These are not incremental problems — they sit at the frontier of applied AI research, with real operational stakes and the potential to reshape how the energy industry is built.

In this role, you will research novel approaches to these problems, collaborate closely with domain experts and engineering partners, and see your work through to deployed systems that actively inform decisions — across construction, capital planning, security operations, and beyond. You will work alongside some of the top nuclear industry experts in the field, a team of PhD-level researchers, and software engineers dedicated to bringing your models into production — giving you the domain depth, technical support, and collaborative environment to do your best work. This is a place to make major contributions on a small but growing team, develop your skills across a remarkable range of hard problems, and be part of something that genuinely matters.

Responsibilities

Research & Modeling

  • Problem Formulation: Translate complex operational processes into well-defined research problems; identify the right modeling approach for each domain and build the case for why it will work in practice.
  • Simulation & Evaluation: Build simulation environments that faithfully represent our operational processes — construction scheduling, portfolio sequencing, security operations — and can be used to train, evaluate, and iterate on decision-making models.
  • Empirical Research: Design rigorous experiments, maintain reproducible codebases, and communicate results clearly in internal reports and, where the research warrants it, external publications.

Some of the exciting topics you are likely to work on include:

Construction Schedule Optimization

  • Schedule Optimization: Develop models that optimize construction scheduling across multiple concurrent sites — minimizing schedule variance, resource idle time, and cascading delays across a growing fleet of projects.
  • Dynamic Rescheduling: Design approaches that adapt scheduling decisions in real time to disruptions — supply chain delays, labor fluctuations, permitting hold-ups — learning from historical project data to improve over time.

Site Portfolio Optimization

  • Portfolio Decision Systems: Build models that inform how we sequence site development and allocate capital across a growing fleet — accounting for regulatory milestones, capital constraints, and correlated risks across sites.
  • Uncertainty Quantification: Develop approaches that account for uncertainty in key inputs — permitting timelines, cost distributions, grid demand forecasts — to produce portfolio decisions with bounded downside.

Security Operations

  • Security Intelligence: Build models for alert prioritization, anomaly detection, and patrol scheduling that support physical and cyber security operations across a distributed multi-site infrastructure.
  • Human-in-the-Loop Design: Design systems where models and human analysts share decision authority appropriately — communicating uncertainty clearly and degrading safely when operating outside familiar conditions.

Production Deployment & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Model Deployment: Collaborate with engineering to define how models are served, monitored, updated, and overridden in production — ensuring deployed systems are reliable, maintainable, and trusted by the teams that use them.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Present research results and system performance to operations, security, and leadership stakeholders; translate findings into actionable operational recommendations.

Experience

  • Research Foundation: PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Operations Research, Economics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related quantitative field — or MS with a demonstrable track record of independent research output (publications, patents, or equivalent deployed systems).
  • Reinforcement Learning Depth: Hands-on experience implementing and evaluating deep RL algorithms; fluency in policy gradient methods (PPO, TRPO, SAC), value-based approaches (DQN variants, IQL), and the tradeoffs between model-free and model-based RL.
  • Simulation Engineering: Experience building RL training environments; demonstrated ability to translate complex real-world operational processes into tractable MDP formulations with appropriate state/action/reward design.
  • Software Engineering: Production-quality Python; deep learning frameworks (PyTorch); version control, testing, and reproducibility practices expected of research code that ships into production systems.
  • Startup Agility: A demonstrated ability to operate in a fast-moving environment where problem definitions evolve, priorities shift, and hands-on technical contribution — not just research direction — is expected at all levels.

Preferred Experience

  • Offline / Batch RL: IQL, CQL, TD3+BC, Decision Transformer, or similar methods — directly relevant given limited online interaction in our deployment environments.
  • Combinatorial Optimization + ML: Graph neural networks for scheduling or routing (GCN, attention-based), neural combinatorial optimization, or hybrid learned/exact solver approaches.
  • Multi-Agent RL: MADDPG, QMIX, MAPPO, or related methods for multi-site coordination and adversarial security formulations.
  • Stochastic / Robust Optimization: CVaR-constrained RL, distributionally robust MDPs, or chance-constrained programming for decision-making under uncertainty.
  • Production RL Deployment: Experience monitoring and retraining RL systems post-deployment, including distribution shift detection and safe policy update procedures.
  • Domain Exposure: Construction project management, infrastructure operations, energy industry, electricity markets, nuclear power, industrial control systems, or physical/cyber security for critical infrastructure.
  • Game Theory: Familiarity with game-theoretic frameworks — strategic interactions, mechanism design, adversarial dynamics, or equilibrium concepts — provides useful modeling perspective for problems where multiple decision-makers interact, compete, or coordinate.
  • Behavioral Science: An understanding of how people actually make decisions — including cognitive biases, bounded rationality, and responses to uncertainty — is valuable when building systems that work alongside human decision-makers.
  • Research Program Leadership: 2-5 years of post-PhD research experience with demonstrated ownership of a research program: defining scope, setting methodology under uncertainty, and being accountable for both published results and deployed system quality.
  • Publication Track Record: Publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAMAS, or equivalent); experience driving a team’s external research agenda and identifying which contributions warrant external dissemination.
  • Mentorship & Team Development: Experience formally mentoring PhD-level researchers or interns; ability to define research objectives for others and provide substantive technical guidance on experimental design and problem formulation.
  • Cross-Functional Technical Leadership: Experience making research architecture decisions that span research and engineering — model serving, retraining triggers, monitoring design — and communicating technical direction to non-technical senior stakeholders.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation packages
  • 401k with company match
  • Medical, dental, vision plans
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays

The estimated starting salary range for this role is $150,000 - $173,000 annually less applicable withholdings and deductions, paid on a bi-weekly basis. The actual salary offered may vary based on relevant factors as determined in the Company’s discretion, which may include experience, qualifications, tenure, skill set, availability of qualified candidates, geographic location, certifications held, and other criteria deemed pertinent to the particular role.

  • Review inspection and test procedures and acceptance criteria for nuclear systems and components; verify design outputs meet specified requirements.

  • Support the QAPD and parent-suite artifacts maintained audit-ready, and the phased QA plans for Services, BOO project development, and JV support.
  • Identify and report conditions adverse to quality promptly through the CAP; feed procedure-production status and quality metrics into the QA metrics pack and the CNO performance-indicator set.

  • Strong technical writing and cross-functional coordination — can pull SME input from any department and drive a document through a multi-reviewer approval chain on schedule.

About the role

The Senior Vice President, Deployment is TNC’s fleet-level owner of nuclear project execution from FEL-3 through fuel load. This role owns the company’s deployment methodology, EPC contractor relationships, construction execution, and commissioning capability across all TNC projects in the pipeline. It is one of the most consequential hires TNC will make.

TNC’s Build-Own-Operate model depends on a deployment capability that is repeatable, credible, and improving with each project. The SVP, Deployment is responsible for building that capability from the ground up — establishing the systems, processes, standards, and team that will allow TNC to execute nuclear construction projects at fleet scale. This is not a role for someone who wants to run one project. It is a role for someone who wants to build the operational infrastructure that makes TNC a world-class nuclear developer and operator.

TNC’s development-to-operations pipeline is structured around three sequential phases with defined handoff periods. This role enters during FEL-3 — the final pre-FID development phase — working alongside the SVP, Project Development during the transition. From FID through commissioning and fuel load, this role owns the project. At fuel load, the SVP, Deployment transitions accountability to the SVP, Operations during a defined handoff period. Managing both of these transitions well is as important as managing the construction work in between.

As TNC’s organizational structure matures and the company scales, reporting lines may be adjusted to reflect evolving business needs — the scope and accountabilities of this role are not contingent on any single reporting structure.

Responsibilities

Deployment Methodology & Fleet Capability

The SVP, Deployment’s first and most enduring responsibility is building TNC’s deployment capability as a repeatable, scalable organizational competency. Individual project performance matters; fleet-level deployment capability matters more.

  • Establish TNC’s deployment methodology — the standardized processes, playbooks, stage gate frameworks, and decision-making structures that govern how TNC executes nuclear construction projects. This methodology is a competitive asset; it must be built deliberately and improved with every project.
  • Own the lessons learned function across deployment projects — ensuring that every project execution experience, whether successful or not, is captured, analyzed, and incorporated into the next project’s execution plan. TNC’s Vogtle-era experience is the starting point; the SVP, Deployment builds on it systematically.
  • Develop and maintain the deployment team’s organizational capability — recruiting, developing, and retaining the engineering, construction, and project management talent that TNC needs to execute at fleet scale. The team this person builds will determine what TNC can accomplish over the next decade.
  • Establish TNC’s quality standards for deployment activities — coordinating with the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Training to ensure deployment execution meets NQA-1 requirements and positions TNC as a demonstrably credible nuclear constructor.

FEL-3 Entry & FID Preparation

FEL-3 is the phase where development transitions to deployment. The SVP, Deployment enters during this phase, working alongside the SVP, Project Development during the handoff period. Entering too late creates execution risk at FID; entering well creates the conditions for a strong construction start.

  • Engage during FEL-3 on all active TNC projects — assessing site readiness, construction execution strategy, EPC contractor selection, and the completeness of the technical and commercial package required to support a credible FID.
  • Own EPC contractor selection and contracting strategy — from pre-qualification through contract execution. The EPC contractor relationship is the single most consequential vendor relationship in TNC’s deployment model; the SVP, Deployment owns it at the fleet level.
  • Validate the FEL-3 package from a deployment perspective — confirming that the project schedule, cost estimate, Division of Responsibilities, and construction execution strategy are credible and executable before FID is recommended.
  • Coordinate with the SVP, Project Development on the FEL-3 handoff — ensuring a complete, documented transition of project accountability from the development team to the deployment team. The handoff is not a single event; it is a managed transition with defined milestones and shared accountability during the overlap period.

Construction Execution

From FID through construction completion, the SVP, Deployment owns the project. EPC contractor performance, schedule, cost, quality, and safety are all accountability items for this role — not just oversight items.

  • Own EPC contractor performance across all active construction projects — holding the contractor accountable to schedule, cost, quality, and safety standards through rigorous owner oversight. TNC is the owner; the SVP, Deployment ensures TNC acts like one.
  • Maintain schedule and cost discipline across the deployment portfolio — providing the President/CNO with an accurate, current view of project status, risks, and decisions required. No surprises on cost or schedule; early warning and honest assessment are the standard.
  • Own the construction quality program in coordination with the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Training — ensuring that TNC’s quality standards are implemented and enforced throughout construction. Quality failures in construction are the most expensive problems TNC can have.
  • Manage regulatory interface during construction in coordination with the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Training — ensuring NRC oversight, inspection readiness, and regulatory commitments are met throughout the construction phase. No unilateral NRC engagement without coordinating with the regulatory function.
  • Ensure safety conscious work environment standards are maintained across all TNC construction sites — TNC’s safety culture during construction is a direct reflection of the operating culture it intends to maintain during operations.

Commissioning & Fuel Load Handoff

Commissioning and fuel load is the deployment phase’s exit transition. The SVP, Deployment owns this phase and manages the structured handoff to the SVP, Operations. A clean handoff is as important as a successful construction program.

  • Own commissioning execution — managing the transition from construction completion to operational readiness, coordinating with the SVP, Operations to ensure the operating organization is ready to receive the plant at fuel load.
  • Manage the fuel load handoff to the SVP, Operations — a defined transition period with shared accountability between Deployment and Operations. The handoff includes physical plant readiness, documentation completeness, staff qualification status, and regulatory authorization. Neither party declares completion unilaterally.
  • Ensure all pre-operational testing, system walkdowns, and commissioning milestones are complete and documented before the fuel load handoff is executed — the SVP, Operations receives a plant that is ready to operate, not one that requires further deployment work.

Commercial & Investor Interface

  • Support the President/CNO and President/CFO in investor, lender, and partner conversations that require deployment expertise — construction schedule credibility, EPC contractor strategy, cost estimates, and execution risk assessments are all areas where the SVP, Deployment’s judgment directly affects TNC’s financing and commercial outcomes.
  • Support DOE LPO and other government financing engagements that require construction execution credibility — coordinating with the CFO organization on the technical inputs that underpin TNC’s financing applications.
  • Coordinate with the SVP, Project Development on project pipeline prioritization — deployment capacity constraints should inform which projects advance to FEL-3 and when. The deployment organization’s bandwidth is a real constraint on TNC’s growth rate.

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in nuclear construction, with direct accountability for large-scale nuclear plant construction or major construction restart at the project director, project executive, or equivalent level.
  • Direct experience managing EPC contractors as an owner’s representative on a nuclear construction project — contract management, performance oversight, change order discipline, and schedule recovery experience required.
  • Deep familiarity with NRC construction oversight, inspection programs, and the regulatory environment governing nuclear new build — direct NRC interface experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience with AP1000 or equivalent Generation III+ reactor technology construction strongly preferred — familiarity with Westinghouse’s design documentation, construction methodology, and regulatory interface is a structural advantage.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and lead large, multi-disciplinary project organizations — this role requires both the technical credibility to lead engineers and construction professionals and the leadership capability to build a new organizational function from the ground up.
  • Strong commercial judgment — able to engage credibly with investors, lenders, and commercial partners on construction execution strategy, cost estimates, and schedule commitments. This is not a purely technical role.
  • Nuclear safety culture leader — establishes and maintains the safety conscious work environment standards that TNC intends to carry from construction through operations.

TNC’s Build-Own-Operate model is only as credible as TNC’s operating capability. Investors, regulators, offtakers, and partners will assess TNC’s long-term viability based in large part on whether TNC can field a world-class operating organization. The SVP, Operations is the person who builds that organization — establishing the nuclear safety culture, the operating standards, the staffing model, and the regulatory posture that will govern TNC’s plants for decades.

This role has two equally important mandates. The first is internal — build TNC’s operating organization, receive plants from the Deployment team at fuel load, and operate them safely, reliably, and efficiently over their full licensed life. The second is external — develop and deliver operational readiness services and planning support for partners and utilities who are building their own operating organizations or planning to operate their own facilities. These two mandates reinforce each other: TNC’s internal operating excellence is the proof point that makes the external services credible.

TNC’s development-to-operations pipeline moves through three sequential phases. This role enters during the commissioning and fuel load phase — working alongside the SVP, Deployment during the handoff period — and then owns the plant from commercial operation through end of life. The fuel load handoff is not a single event; it is a managed transition with shared accountability and defined milestones.

As TNC’s organizational structure matures and the company scales, reporting lines may be adjusted to reflect evolving business needs — the scope and accountabilities of this role are not contingent on any single reporting structure.

Operations Organization Build

The most urgent mandate of this role is building TNC’s operating organization before it is needed. Operating organizations take years to build, qualify, and license. The time to start is now.

  • Design and build TNC’s nuclear operating organization from the ground up — defining the structure, staffing model, qualification requirements, and training program that will allow TNC to receive and operate its first plant at fuel load.
  • Establish TNC’s nuclear safety culture from the first hire — the operating culture that takes root in the early days of organization-building is the culture that governs plant safety for the life of the facility. This is not a compliance exercise; it is the foundation of everything TNC does as an operator.
  • Develop the operating staffing plan for TNC’s lead project — identifying the number, qualifications, and timeline for licensed and non-licensed operating staff required to support fuel load and initial commercial operations.
  • Coordinate with the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Training on the training program for TNC’s operating organization — operator qualification, simulator training, and ongoing training program development are a shared accountability between Operations and the regulatory/training function.
  • Establish TNC’s operating procedures program — emergency operating procedures, abnormal operating procedures, and normal operating procedures are the foundation of licensed operations. These must be in place and validated before fuel load.

Fuel Load Handoff & Initial Operations

Receiving the plant from the Deployment team at fuel load is one of the most complex transitions in the nuclear lifecycle. The SVP, Operations owns TNC’s readiness for that transition.

  • Engage during commissioning alongside the SVP, Deployment — ensuring the operating organization is ready to receive the plant, that all pre-operational testing is complete, and that the plant’s technical documentation is sufficient to support licensed operations.
  • Own the fuel load readiness assessment — confirming that TNC’s operating organization, procedures, staffing, and NRC authorizations are in place before fuel load is authorized. The SVP, Operations does not accept a plant that is not ready to operate.
  • Manage the NRC pre-operational inspection program in coordination with the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Training — ensuring TNC’s operating organization meets all NRC requirements for initial fuel load and plant startup.
  • Lead the initial startup program through initial criticality and power ascension testing to commercial operation — the most consequential operational sequence TNC will execute on each project.

  • Own the outage management program across TNC’s operating fleet — refueling outages, forced outages, and major maintenance outages are the highest-risk and highest-cost events in the operating lifecycle. Outage performance is a direct measure of operational maturity.
  • Maintain TNC’s operating licenses across all facilities — coordinating with the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, Quality & Training on license renewals, technical specification changes, and NRC inspection readiness. The operating license is TNC’s most valuable single asset at each site.
  • Engage with INPO and WANO as TNC’s senior operations representative — TNC will seek INPO accreditation for its training program and will participate fully in the industry peer evaluation process. INPO performance is not a compliance exercise; it is the industry’s benchmark for operating excellence.
  • Develop operating performance metrics and report to the President/CNO on a regular cadence — capacity factor, safety system performance, corrective action program health, and outage performance. The CNO should never be surprised by operating performance.

Operational Readiness Services — External Partners

TNC’s operating capability is a commercial asset as well as an internal necessity. Partners and utilities who are planning to operate nuclear facilities — whether TNC BOO projects or their own — need expert operational readiness support. TNC is positioned to provide it.

  • Develop and deliver operational readiness advisory services for partners and utilities who are building their own operating organizations or planning to operate nuclear facilities — organizational design, staffing model development, procedure program development, training program design, and pre-operational readiness assessments.

The Nuclear Company is seeking a Siting Engineer to serve as the technical owner of a site across its full development life cycle. This role works alongside the Origination group during screening and qualification of candidate sites, then takes the formal handoff of land and the site technical baseline at the FEL 0 admission gate and carries the site through characterization, licensing, and design integration (FEL 1–3) to readiness for construction.

You are the continuity of site knowledge across the Origination/Development boundary: the person who ensures that what was promised at admission is what gets characterized, licensed, and ultimately built. The ideal candidate combines hands-on site characterization experience with working fluency in NRC siting regulations and the discipline to produce licensing-grade documentation inside a stage-gate framework.

Responsibilities

Origination Support & FEL 0 Handoff

  • Provide technical siting support to the Origination group during screening: fatal-flaw assessments, hazard standoff analyses (NRC Regulatory Guide 1.91), buildable-area and cooling water evaluations, and population/exclusion criteria checks (10 CFR Part 100, Regulatory Guide 4.7)
  • Validate candidate site packages against the FEL 0 Entry Boundary Conditions and confirm the technical basis for admission decisions
  • Receive the formal handoff of land control, geospatial baseline, and site technical data at FEL 0 admission, and own that baseline through all subsequent phases

Site Characterization (FEL 1–3)

  • Scope, procure, and manage geotechnical, geological, seismological, hydrological, and ecological investigation programs
  • Stand up and operate site meteorological monitoring programs (Regulatory Guide 1.23) meeting ESP/COL data quality and duration requirements
  • Maintain the site GIS datasets, land control mapping, and survey baseline; manage characterization consultants and field subcontractors

Licensing & Environmental Support

  • Prepare site-related portions of ESP and COL applications under 10 CFR Part 52, including SSAR/FSAR Chapter 2 inputs, consistent with NUREG-0800 and NUREG-1555
  • Provide siting inputs to Environmental Reports and support NRC pre-application engagement, audits, and RAI responses on site matters
  • Reconcile site characteristics against the plant site parameter envelope and manage departures and open items to closure

Construction Transition

  • Translate the characterized site into construction readiness: early site works permitting, site preparation and excavation input packages, geotechnical baseline reports for constructors
  • Support constructability reviews and remain the site technical authority through mobilization, providing site data continuity for construction and ITAAC-relevant verification

AI & Technology

  • Leverage AI-powered tools, GIS platforms, and data analytics to accelerate characterization planning, data review, and decision-making
  • Maintain siting dashboards and databases within NOS to track characterization progress, land confidence, and gate readiness

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Geology, Geotechnical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Environmental Science, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline (Master's preferred)
  • 5+ years of experience in power plant or large industrial facility siting, site characterization, or site licensing/environmental work
  • Working knowledge of 10 CFR Parts 50, 52, and 100, and NRC Regulatory Guides 7, 1.91, and 1.23
  • Hands-on experience scoping or executing field investigation programs (geotechnical, hydrological, meteorological, or seismic)
  • Strong technical writing skills with experience producing licensing-grade or investor-grade documentation
  • Ability to travel regularly to project sites

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with ESP or COL applications, Environmental Reports, or SSAR/FSAR Chapter 2 development
  • Familiarity with large light-water reactor site parameter envelopes (e.g., AP1000)
  • Experience carrying a site into construction: early site works, excavation support, or geotechnical baseline reporting
  • Knowledge of probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) and geologic characterization methodologies
  • GIS proficiency (ArcGIS or equivalent) and experience with geospatial land control analysis
  • Experience working in a stage-gate (FEL) project development framework
  • Professional Engineer (PE) or Professional Geologist (PG) license

About the role

The United States is building nuclear power again, at a scale not attempted in a generation, and The Nuclear Company is leading it. Our Applied Research and AI team works on the open problems that decide how a fleet of plants gets built: sequencing construction across many concurrent sites, allocating capital under deep uncertainty, and keeping a distributed critical infrastructure secure. These are hard problems with real operational stakes, and the work ships into systems that inform real decisions.

You will put reinforcement learning and optimization to work on problems that decide how a fleet of plants gets built: how to sequence construction across many sites, where to place capital under uncertainty, and how to keep a distributed site secure. As a Data Science & Machine Learning Fellow, you formulate the problem, build a simulation or optimization model, evaluate it rigorously, and help move it toward a deployed decision system. You work alongside nuclear industry experts to deliver solutions that inform real decisions and create business value.

This is a 12-week Summer 2027 fellowship (May to August), aligned to the academic calendar. Base location is Washington DC, on-site five days a week, with full housing and relocation for fellows outside the DC metro area.

Responsibilities

  • Problem formulation: translate operational processes (construction scheduling, portfolio sequencing, security operations) into well-defined modeling problems and make the case for the right approach.
  • Simulation and evaluation: build environments that faithfully represent these processes so models can be trained, evaluated, and iterated on.
  • Modeling: develop reinforcement learning, optimization, or forecasting models for schedule optimization, capital allocation under uncertainty, or anomaly detection and alert prioritization.
  • Empirical research: design rigorous experiments, keep reproducible codebases, and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Production path: work with engineering on how models are served, monitored, updated, and safely overridden in production.

Required Experience

  • Currently pursuing an MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Operations Research, Applied Math, Economics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field. Returning to your MS or PhD program after the fellowship (expected graduation December 2027 or later).
  • Production-quality Python and PyTorch, with solid machine learning fundamentals.
  • Hands-on experience (coursework, research, or projects) with at least one of: reinforcement learning, mathematical optimization, simulation and modeling, or time-series forecasting.
  • Able to translate a messy real-world process into a tractable formulation (an MDP with sensible state, action, and reward, or an optimization model) and explain the modeling choice. Running pre-built models on clean benchmarks is not enough.
  • Demonstrated ability to design, implement, and evaluate experiments, with reproducible research practices (version control, testing).
  • This position requires access to information and technology subject to U.S. export controls (including DOE 10 CFR Part 810 and NRC requirements). U.S. Person status (U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident) is required, and TNC does not provide visa sponsorship for these roles.

About the Role

We're seeking a hands-on Supply Chain Manager to own end-to-end supply chain operations for a nuclear plant build, including planning, sourcing, inventory, warehousing, and logistics, while leading the implementation of NetSuite's ERP inventory and supply chain modules. This is a build role: you'll design and stand up the systems and processes from scratch while keeping day-to-day operations running, all within a nuclear quality assurance program where traceability and documentation control are licensing conditions. Please note: This role will support TNC’s greenfield nuclear construction projects and is not assigned to the V.C. Summer project or work being performed through TNC’s related joint venture.

This is a hybrid position based in our downtown Columbia, South Carolina office, with an expected in-office presence of 2-3 days per week. The role has been posted in surrounding markets for visibility, as the hybrid schedule may make the commute workable for candidates living outside the immediate Columbia area.

Responsibilities

Quality Assurance & Regulatory Compliance

  • Operate within a nuclear QA program (10 CFR 50 Appendix B, ASME NQA-1), applying graded QA controls across safety-related, safety-significant, and commercial-grade items; maintain full item traceability (heat/lot numbers, CMTRs, certificates of conformance)
  • Manage commercial-grade dedication (CGD) with Engineering and QA, including QA review and approval of acceptance; enforce counterfeit/suspect item (CFSI) prevention
  • Assist QA in developing procurement document controls so technical, quality, and regulatory requirements flow down to suppliers and sub-tier suppliers and are verified on receipt
  • Assist QA in developing nonconformance, hold, and quarantine processes (QA retains control); support NRC inspections, ITAAC closure, and audit readiness
  • Administer graded storage and preservation requirements (NQA-1 storage levels), including shelf-life and rotation programs, calibration status of controlled items, and foreign material exclusion (FME) discipline

NetSuite ERP Implementation

  • Own configuration and rollout of Inventory Management, Demand Planning, and Work Orders modules from current state to go-live, within corporate ERP governance and Finance-approved change control for GL-impacting configuration.
  • Build the item master, multi-level BOMs, UOM framework, and location/bin structures
  • Define and document planning parameters: reorder points, safety stock, lot sizing, planning horizon, and time fence rules
  • Partner with Finance on inventory accounting configuration: costing method (set by Accounting), landed cost allocation, standard cost revisions, variance accounts, WIP , COGS, and project (CWIP) cost mapping, and inventory GL reconciliation
  • Configure nuclear quality attributes (Q-list flags, lot/serial tracking) and document retention tied to items and transactions
  • Lead data migration/cutover, UAT, SOPs, and user training; own the post-go-live enhancement backlog

Demand & Supply Planning

  • Run demand planning, MRP/supply planning, and a monthly S&OP cadence
  • Manage inventory investment (turns, days of supply, fill rate); own SKU replenishment strategy
  • Lead first-article and long-lead component readiness; manage engineering change orders through the supply chain, including inventory exposure, run-out plans, and supplier requalification

Inventory, Warehousing & Logistics

  • Drive inventory accuracy via cycle counting; own physical inventory reconciliation to GL on the monthly close calendar with adjustments posted timely and root-caused
  • Define and manage receiving, inspection routing, put-away, and kitting and material issue to work packages in the field; manage inbound and outbound logistics, freight, and trade compliance
  • Enforce PO and receiving discipline supporting AP three-way match: timely and accurate receipts, month-end receiving cutoff, and goods-received-not-invoiced (GRNI) accrual support; maintain segregation of duties across requisitioning, receiving, and payment
  • Manage excess/obsolete inventory disposition (quarterly E&O reserve analysis to Finance; write-offs approved per delegation of authority) and 3PL relationships

Reporting & Leadership

  • Build KPI dashboards and reporting in NetSuite
  • Use AI and automation to eliminate manual supply chain work; own the quality of supply chain data feeding Nuclear Operating System (NOS)
  • Own the supply chain budget and inventory investment plan, with monthly variance reporting and reforecasts to Finance
  • Mentor and develop supply chain, purchasing, and warehouse staff

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, operations, industrial engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience
  • 5+ years progressive supply chain experience, including 2+ years in management/team lead
  • Hands-on experience configuring NetSuite inventory/supply chain functionality (not just using it)
  • Strong grasp of BOMs, multi-UOM setup, and inventory accounting (standard cost, variances, landed cost, WIP/COGS)
  • Experience running demand planning/MRP with a track record of improving forecast accuracy or turns
  • Multi-location/entity inventory experience (transfer orders, in-transit inventory)
  • Working knowledge of domestic and international logistics, freight cost management, and import/export compliance
  • Experience controlling material under a nuclear QA program or comparable regulated regime (AS9100, defense, ASME Section III)
  • Command of traceability/documentation control (CMTRs, certs of conformance, nonconformance processes)
  • Experience managing suppliers against written quality requirements with sub-tier flow-down
  • Budget ownership experience; advanced Excel; strong cross-functional communication
  • Demonstrated use of AI and automation to remove manual work from supply chain or ERP processes

Preferred Qualifications

  • Full ownership of a NetSuite implementation from design through post-go-live
  • APICS/ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP)
  • Manufacturing/assembly environment experience (make-to-stock and make-to-order)
  • Direct nuclear new-build, major modification, or SMR project experience (ITAAC documentation)
  • Familiarity with CGD, CFSI, 10 CFR Part 21, ASME Section III procurement, N-stamp/NUPIC/NIAC audit programs, and nuclear export control (10 CFR Part 810, NRC Part 110)
  • Familiarity with NetSuite Advanced Manufacturing, WMS, Demand Planning, or third-party planning tools
  • Lean/Six Sigma trainin

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation packages
  • 401k with company match
  • Medical, dental, vision plans
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays

  • Institutional readiness. Build a scalable FP&A function with the forecasting, guidance, expectations modeling, and reporting cadence needed for the company’s next stage of growth - working with Controllership and External Reporting, and help stand up the systems and processes to get there.
  • Team & operating model. Lead and develop the corporate FP&A team; build a scalable, tech / AI-enabled planning function with wide spans and few layers.

  • 12+ years of progressive FP&A / finance experience, including a senior corporate FP&A leadership role (Head of FP&A, VP FP&A, or equivalent).

About the role

The Nuclear Company is seeking a Vice President, Engineering to lead the engineering organization responsible for the successful development and execution of a fleet of nuclear power plants.

This is a senior leadership role for an experienced nuclear professional who has spent significant time in the realities of the industry—design, construction, commissioning, operations, major projects, and/or asset management—and understands what it takes to move a nuclear project from engineering definition into construction and ultimately safe, reliable operation.

The VP, Engineering will build and lead an owner's engineering organization capable of integrating reactor technology, architect-engineer partners, EPC organizations, suppliers, utilities, regulators, and construction teams into a disciplined and repeatable delivery model, providing full lifecycle project support from early design through construction, commissioning, and operations.

We are looking for a builder, operator, and engineering leader—someone who combines deep nuclear judgment with the urgency and pragmatism required to build the next generation of American nuclear infrastructure.

Responsibilities

Lead the Engineering Organization

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary nuclear engineering organization.
  • Establish the engineering management system, organizational structure, technical authorities, design responsibilities, and decision rights required to execute multiple nuclear projects.
  • Recruit and develop leaders across key disciplines including mechanical, electrical, civil/structural, I&C, systems, configuration management, design engineering, and engineering programs.
  • Create a culture of technical rigor, accountability, speed, and continuous improvement.

Own Engineering Execution

  • Provide executive leadership for engineering across the full project lifecycle—from site development and design through procurement, construction, commissioning, turnover, and operations.
  • Establish engineering plans, priorities, schedules, deliverables, and performance metrics aligned with overall project execution.
  • Ensure engineering is sufficiently mature to support procurement and construction when required, minimizing field changes, rework, and schedule disruption.
  • Drive resolution of complex technical issues and ensure engineering decisions balance nuclear safety, constructability, operability, cost, schedule, and lifecycle performance.
  • Establish disciplined design-change, configuration-management, technical-document, and engineering-change-control processes.

Build for Constructability and Operability

  • Bring an operator’s and constructor’s mindset to engineering decisions.
  • Ensure designs incorporate lessons learned from operating nuclear plants and recent new-build programs.
  • Integrate construction sequencing, modularization, supply-chain realities, commissioning requirements, maintenance, reliability, and long-term plant operations into design decisions.
  • Partner closely with Construction, Project Management, Supply Chain, Quality, Licensing, Operations, and Commissioning to eliminate organizational handoffs and solve problems as one integrated project team.
  • Champion standardization and resist unnecessary project-specific customization.

Manage Engineering Partners and Suppliers

  • Serve as the senior technical interface with reactor technology providers, architect-engineers, EPC partners, utilities, major equipment suppliers, and other engineering organizations.
  • Establish clear scopes, interfaces, deliverables, technical requirements, and accountability across engineering partners.
  • Evaluate engineering performance and intervene quickly when technical, organizational, or execution issues threaten project outcomes.
  • Ensure supplier engineering and vendor technical information are integrated into the overall plant design on schedule.

Create a Repeatable Fleet Model

  • Develop engineering processes that support a fleet-build strategy rather than a series of one-off projects.
  • Capture and systematically incorporate lessons learned from each project into subsequent units.
  • Drive design standardization, repeatability, configuration control, and reuse of engineering work products.
  • Identify opportunities to use technology, data, automation, and AI to improve engineering productivity, knowledge management, design assurance, and decision-making.
  • Build institutional engineering capability that compounds as the fleet grows.

Provide Executive Technical Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor to the executive leadership team on engineering risk, project readiness, technical strategy, and major project decisions.
  • Clearly communicate complex engineering issues and tradeoffs to executives, boards, investors, utilities, regulators, and project partners.
  • Establish an environment where issues are surfaced early, challenged constructively, and resolved decisively.
  • Maintain an uncompromising commitment to nuclear safety, quality, and regulatory compliance while continuously challenging the organization to execute better and faster.

Experience

  • 20+ years of engineering and leadership experience in the nuclear power industry, major power generation, or similarly complex regulated infrastructure.
  • Significant experience with commercial nuclear power plants and/or nuclear new-build projects.
  • Demonstrated leadership across multiple phases of the nuclear lifecycle, including engineering, construction, commissioning, operations, major projects, or asset management.
  • Deep understanding of nuclear plant systems, engineering programs, configuration management, design control, and industry standards.
  • Strong working knowledge of the interfaces between engineering, licensing, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operations.
  • Experience leading large multidisciplinary engineering teams and external engineering organizations.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage architect-engineers, OEMs, EPC organizations, utilities, and major suppliers.
  • Experience resolving complex technical and project execution challenges where safety, quality, cost, and schedule must all be considered.
  • Strong understanding of the lessons learned from recent U.S. and international nuclear construction programs.
  • Proven ability to develop people, build organizations, establish processes, and create accountability in rapidly growing environments.
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline; advanced degree and/or Professional Engineer license preferred.
